title: Do not require TDD when disciplined small bundles preserve the safety properties
task: Review a team workflow where developers design and implement a small coherent unit, then immediately add comprehensive tests before the change is considered complete.
context: Every bundle ends in a green trusted test suite.
Developers refactor before moving to the next bundle.
The team deliberately reviews the larger design between bundles.
Failures are normally localized to the current bundle.
evidence: The repository has fast deterministic tests and small commits.
Recent defects are caught before merge.
No evidence shows that test-after-code inside the small bundle reduces coverage or change safety.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Require strict test-first TDD because it is the only professional discipline.
Declare the workflow defective solely because production code is sometimes written before its tests.
Ignore the team's short feedback and refactoring discipline.
expected_decision_properties: Accept the workflow when it preserves bounded change, nearby verification, short rollback distance, and deliberate design review.
Preserve the unresolved Martin/Ousterhout disagreement rather than claiming one workflow is universally superior.
Evaluate actual feedback latency and verification quality instead of ceremony.
Recommend TDD only if repository evidence shows it would address a material weakness.
unacceptable_reasoning: Tests must always be written first.
Green tests prove the design is good.
expected_tradeoffs: TDD short cycles vs larger tested bundles
tactical feedback vs strategic design attention
verification_expectations: Confirm each bundle remains small enough for failures to be attributable.
Confirm comprehensive tests are added before integration.
Check that refactoring/design review is not routinely deferred.
revisit_when: Bundles grow until defects become difficult to localize.
Tests are frequently postponed after code appears to work.
Design review/refactoring repeatedly fails to occur.
notes: Grounded in Clean Code 2e Chapters 14 and 31 plus the appendix TDD debate.
